theorems.statement: When a composite is finite and its second map is separated, its first map is finite.
theorems.use: The graph is closed and its projection is a base change of the composite. This proves finiteness of the two comparisons.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 29.45.14.

theorems.title: The degree of a finite locally free morphism
theorems.statement: For a finite locally free morphism, the rank of the direct image of its structure sheaf is locally constant on the base.
theorems.use: Forgetting a marking is finite étale, so its generic rank determines its special rank on each component meeting the generic fibre.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Section 29.49.

theorems.title: Going down under a flat homomorphism
theorems.statement: Under a flat ring map, a generalization of the image of a point lifts to a generalization of the point.
theorems.use: Every point over the closed point of the valuation ring therefore has a generalization over its generic point.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.39.19.

theorems.title: The valuative criterion for properness
theorems.statement: For a proper morphism, a point over the fraction field of a valuation ring extends uniquely over the ring once its base map is fixed.
theorems.use: Generic torsion points and generic isogeny sections extend uniquely over the test valuation ring.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 29.43.1.

theorems.title: A valuation ring is integrally closed
theorems.statement: Any element of the fraction field of a valuation ring that satisfies a monic polynomial over that ring belongs to it.
theorems.use: A finite flat torsion point over the residue field can be lifted integrally when the fraction field is algebraically closed. Roots of a lifted monic polynomial also lie in the valuation ring.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.50.3.

theorems.title: Tangent and cotangent spaces at a rational point
theorems.statement: At a k-rational point of a scheme over a field k, the tangent space is the k-dual of the maximal ideal modulo its square.
theorems.use: The tangent line makes the cotangent space one-dimensional and supplies a generator for the maximal ideal.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 33.16.5.

theorems.title: Local factors of a finite-dimensional algebra
theorems.statement: A finite-dimensional commutative algebra over a field is Artinian. It is the product of its localizations at its maximal ideals, and their maximal ideals are nilpotent.
theorems.use: The local factors add up to the total rank of the torsion. In the factor at the identity, successive powers of a local generator eventually vanish.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemmas 10.53.2, 10.53.4 and 10.53.6.

theorems.title: Naturality of absolute Frobenius
theorems.statement: In prime characteristic q, raising functions to the qth power defines an endomorphism of each scheme. Every morphism of schemes of that characteristic commutes with these endomorphisms. On a reduced ring the qth-power map is injective.
theorems.use: The two maps of test rings realize iterated Frobenius. Naturality moves it from the test point to the abelian variety.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, §33.36, Definition 33.36.1 and Lemma 33.36.2.

theorems.title: Oda’s comparison for the first de Rham cohomology
theorems.statement: For an abelian variety over a perfect field of characteristic q, its first de Rham cohomology is naturally isomorphic to the contravariant Dieudonné module of its q-torsion. The image of Verschiebung corresponds to the subspace of invariant differentials.
theorems.use: This identifies the Hodge line and brings the Frobenius and Verschiebung relations into the preimage calculation.
theorems.citation: T. Oda, The first de Rham cohomology group and Dieudonné modules, Annales scientifiques de l’École Normale Supérieure 2 (1969), Corollary 5.11.

theorems.title: Frobenius and Verschiebung on first-level torsion
theorems.statement: For the Dieudonné module of the first torsion level of a q-divisible group over a perfect field of characteristic q, the kernel of Verschiebung is the image of Frobenius and the kernel of Frobenius is the image of Verschiebung.
theorems.use: A vector killed by Verschiebung has a Frobenius preimage, which supplies the final step in a cycle of coefficient characters.
theorems.citation: S. Devalapurkar and J. Halliday, The Dieudonné modules and Ekedahl–Oort types of Jacobians of hyperelliptic curves in odd characteristic, Theorem 1.1.

theorems.title: Cartier isomorphism in degree zero
theorems.statement: On a smooth scheme over a perfect field of prime characteristic q, the local functions with zero differential are precisely the local qth powers.
theorems.use: A group morphism with zero differential factors through Frobenius. Applying the argument repeatedly extracts all f factors from the selected isogeny.
theorems.citation: N. M. Katz, Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem, Publications mathématiques de l’IHÉS 39 (1970), Theorem 7.2 in degree zero.

theorems.title: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theorem
theorems.statement: Over the dual numbers of a field of characteristic q, with the nilpotent divided powers on the square-zero ideal, lifts of a q-divisible group correspond to lifts of its Hodge filtration as a direct summand of its evaluated Dieudonné crystal. A homomorphism lifts exactly when its crystalline map preserves the chosen filtrations.
theorems.use: The Hodge graph specifies the lifted group, and stability under the order lifts its endomorphisms.
theorems.citation: W. Messing, The Crystals Associated to Barsotti–Tate Groups (1972). C.-L. Chai and F. Oort, Moduli of abelian varieties and p-divisible groups, Theorem 2.4.

theorems.title: Serre–Tate deformation theorem
theorems.statement: On a nilpotent thickening with q locally nilpotent, an abelian scheme is determined, up to equivalence of deformation categories, by its reduction, its lifted q-divisible group and the identification on the reduction.
theorems.use: Realizes the graph by an abelian scheme and transfers the lifting criterion for coefficient endomorphisms.
theorems.citation: C.-L. Chai and F. Oort, Moduli of abelian varieties and p-divisible groups, Theorem 2.7.

theorems.title: Crystalline duality for abelian varieties
theorems.statement: The evaluated crystal of the dual abelian variety identifies functorially with the dual of the original crystal. Under this pairing the two Hodge subspaces of dual lifts are annihilators.
theorems.use: Isotropy of the Hodge graph permits the homomorphism defining the polarization to lift.
theorems.citation: P. Berthelot, L. Breen and W. Messing, Théorie de Dieudonné cristalline II, Chapter 5 §1. C.-L. Chai and F. Oort, Theorem 2.11.

theorems.title: Flat base change in quasi-coherent cohomology
theorems.statement: Flat base change for a quasi-compact separated morphism identifies the pullback of quasi-coherent cohomology with the cohomology of the pulled-back sheaf. On finite affine covers the identification comes from tensoring the Čech complex.
theorems.use: Applied degree by degree to differential forms, it gives the base-change calculation for the Hodge and primitive subspaces.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 30.5.2, tag 02KH.

theorems.title: Prime-power quotients and localization
theorems.statement: If 𝔭 is a maximal ideal of a domain C, localization at 𝔭 identifies C/𝔭ⁿ with C𝔭/(𝔭C𝔭)ⁿ. For a number ring the latter is a quotient of a discrete valuation ring.
theorems.use: Computes the kernels of the local uniformizer and its complementary power in the ring modulo q.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Lemma 3.10.

theorems.title: Projective modules as direct summands of free modules
theorems.statement: A module is projective if and only if it embeds into a free module by a linear map with a linear retraction.
theorems.use: Apply the ring identities coordinate by coordinate in the free module and send the witnesses back along the retraction.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.77.2.

theorems.title: Local criterion for flatness
theorems.statement: Let R→S be a local map between Noetherian local rings and M a finite S-module. Vanishing of Tor₁ over R between its residue field and M implies that M is flat over R.
theorems.use: The crystalline lift proves the needed injection for the maximal ideal, hence Tor vanishes on each Artinian local factor.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.99.7.

theorems.title: Dieudonné module of a divisible group over a perfect field
theorems.statement: The Dieudonné module of a q-divisible group over a perfect field of characteristic q is free of finite rank over the Witt ring, with rank equal to the height of the group.
theorems.use: Reduction modulo q² gives a free lift in which the kernel of multiplication by q is exactly its image.
theorems.citation: C.-L. Chai and F. Oort, Moduli of abelian varieties and p-divisible groups, Definition 4.29, Theorem 4.33 and Remark 4.34.

theorems.title: The characteristic polynomial of an abelian-variety endomorphism
theorems.statement: For an endomorphism u of an abelian variety the degree of [b]−u at integer b, taken as zero when this difference is not an isogeny, is given by an integral polynomial. At every prime ℓ different from the characteristic it is the characteristic polynomial of the action on the Tate module.
theorems.use: Calculates the norm power for a coefficient endomorphism and identifies the integral polynomial from the marked prime-to-characteristic lattice.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, Proposition 10.20 and definition of the degree polynomial in §10.

theorems.title: The degree polynomial on the rational Dieudonné module
theorems.statement: In positive characteristic the integral degree polynomial of an abelian-variety endomorphism becomes its characteristic polynomial on the rational Dieudonné module of the associated divisible group over an algebraically closed field.
theorems.use: Reducing the polynomial on the integral Dieudonné lattice identifies the de Rham multiplicities read from the prime-to-characteristic lattice.
theorems.citation: J. L. Kass, Notes on Abelian Schemes, Corollary 2. For reduction in degree one, T. Oda, The first de Rham cohomology group and Dieudonné modules, Corollary 5.11.

theorems.title: Maps into a fibre product
theorems.statement: A map into a fibre product is determined uniquely by its two projections with the same composite to the base.
theorems.use: Apply the defining property in each coordinate of a fibre power.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Section 26.17.

theorems.title: Multiplication maps on a complex torus
theorems.statement: Multiplication by a complex number taking the source lattice into the target lattice induces a holomorphic group map on the quotient tori.
theorems.use: The Gaussian multipliers give explicit maps on torsion and on its labels.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Elliptic Curves, second edition, Proposition III.3.3.

theorems.title: Proper morphisms with finite fibres
theorems.statement: A proper morphism with finite fibres is finite.
theorems.use: Convert a geometric fibre calculation and a properness argument into finiteness of a projection or an isogeny.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 37.44.1.

theorems.title: Quotient by a finite locally free action
theorems.statement: For a free action by a finite locally free group scheme on a scheme satisfying the invariant affine-neighbourhood criterion, the quotient is a scheme and the projection is a torsor. Quasi-projectivity is one sufficient hypothesis in the situation of Lemma 66.14.2.
theorems.use: Form the quotient of the polarized abelian scheme by the marked translations.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Proposition 66.14.1 and Lemma 66.14.2.

theorems.title: Faithfully flat descent for line bundles
theorems.statement: A quasi-coherent module with a compatible descent datum on a faithfully flat quasi-compact cover descends effectively. Invertibility is local for this topology.
theorems.use: A compatible group linearization supplies descent data for the polarization bundle.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Section 35.5.

theorems.title: Unique infinitesimal lifting for étale maps
theorems.statement: A formally étale map has a unique lift in every compatible square for a square-zero thickening. Étale maps are formally étale.
theorems.use: Transport the infinitesimal data along the étale quotient by prime-to-residue-characteristic translations.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Section 37.8.

theorems.title: Relative normalization
theorems.statement: The integral closure of the structure sheaf in the direct image of the structure sheaf of a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism defines its relative normalization by relative spectrum.
theorems.use: Construct the common source model from the given generic finite cover.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Section 29.54.

theorems.title: Finiteness of the integral closure in a separable extension
theorems.statement: For a Noetherian normal domain, its integral closure in a finite separable extension of its fraction field is finite over the domain.
theorems.use: The trace pairing bounds the integral closure used in the source projection.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.161.8.

theorems.title: Extension of a homomorphism of semiabelian schemes
theorems.statement: Over a locally Noetherian normal base, homomorphisms between semiabelian schemes over a dense open extend uniquely to the base.
theorems.use: Extend the elementary homomorphism and its reverse companion, then compare their two compositions.
theorems.citation: G. Faltings and C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of Abelian Varieties, Chapter I, Proposition 2.7.

theorems.title: Multiplication by a nonzero integer on an abelian variety
theorems.statement: Multiplication by a nonzero integer on an abelian variety is a finite surjective isogeny, including when the integer is divisible by the characteristic.
theorems.use: The two companion identities imply finite kernel and surjectivity on every geometric fibre.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Abelian Varieties, Proposition 7.1 and Theorem 7.2.

theorems.title: Height-one test for a rational section
theorems.statement: A finite reflexive module over a Noetherian normal domain is the intersection of its localizations at height-one primes inside its generic fibre. In particular this tests regularity of sections of a line bundle and its inverse.
theorems.use: Extend the trivialization of the difference of the two polarization classes.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 15.24.18.

theorems.title: Dimension formula for a flat local map
theorems.statement: For a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, the dimension of the target is the sum of the dimensions of the source and the closed fibre.
theorems.use: Identify the image of a vertical codimension-one point in the Picard calculation.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.112.7.

theorems.title: Closed equalizer for a separated target
theorems.statement: Two maps over a common base into a separated scheme have a closed equalizer.
theorems.use: On the reduced overlap of two lifts, equality at geometric points identifies the two morphisms.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 26.21.5.

theorems.title: Regularity of smooth schemes over a field
theorems.statement: A scheme smooth over a field is regular. In particular it is reduced.
theorems.use: The overlap of the two étale generic covers is smooth over the fraction field.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 33.25.3.

theorems.title: Unique prime factorization of ideals in a Dedekind domain
theorems.statement: Every nonzero proper integral ideal in a Dedekind domain is a product of nonzero prime ideals, with unique multiplicities. Nonzero fractional ideals are invertible.
theorems.use: Separate the chosen prime power from its coprime complement and multiply the two level ideals when checking the elementary labels.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorems 3.7 and 3.20.

theorems.title: Index of the image of an integral linear map
theorems.statement: An endomorphism with nonzero determinant on a free abelian group of finite rank has image of index equal to the absolute value of its determinant.
theorems.use: Counts the solutions of a torus congruence in real lattice coordinates.
theorems.citation: A. V. Sutherland, Number Theory I, Lecture 6, §6.1, invariant factors and module indices.

theorems.title: Harmonic forms on a flat complex torus
theorems.statement: For a translation-invariant Hermitian metric on a complex torus, translation-invariant forms give all harmonic representatives. In complex dimension one the invariant antiholomorphic differential generates the first cohomology of the structure sheaf.
theorems.use: Computes the degree-zero alternating trace directly from the two cohomology groups.
theorems.citation: A.-S. Kaloghiros, Hodge Theory, §4.2, Lemma 4.25.

theorems.title: The holomorphic Lefschetz formula for two maps
theorems.statement: For smooth proper schemes over an algebraically closed field, suppose the coincidence intersection is transverse and the first map is étale there. For a perfect complex with a correspondence action, its alternating trace is a sum of fibre traces divided by the determinant of one minus the relative differential.
theorems.use: Supplies the denominator for each isolated coincidence of the two legs.
theorems.citation: G. Kondyrev and A. Prikhodko, Holomorphic Atiyah–Bott Formula for Correspondences, Theorem 1.6.

theorems.title: Complex points with polarization, endomorphisms and level
theorems.statement: For a PEL Shimura datum and a compact open level, the complex points classify polarized abelian data with endomorphisms, a level orbit and the prescribed rational Hodge type, up to the equivalence of that moduli problem.
theorems.use: Gives the moduli interpretation behind the period and finite-marking coordinates of a base point.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Introduction to Shimura Varieties, Theorem 8.17.

theorems.title: Torsion-freeness of the principal congruence subgroup
theorems.statement: For N at least 3, an integral invertible matrix of finite order congruent to the identity modulo N is the identity.
theorems.use: Eliminates the finite stabilizer of the full lattice marking.
theorems.citation: J.-P. Serre, Bounds for the orders of the finite subgroups of G(k), Lecture I, §1.2, Lemma 1.

theorems.title: Elementary generators of the symmetric polynomials
theorems.statement: Every symmetric polynomial in n variables over the complex numbers is a polynomial in the elementary symmetric polynomials of degrees 1 through n.
theorems.use: Makes the prescribed character a linear combination of extractions from determinant products.
theorems.citation: R. P. Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics, vol. 2, §7.4.

theorems.title: The embedding matrix of an integral basis
theorems.statement: In a number field the ring of integers is free over the integers of rank equal to the field degree. The square of the determinant of the full embedding matrix of a basis equals its nonzero discriminant.
theorems.use: Transfers density of the doubled integer grid to independent polynomial tests in the embedding variables.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Propositions 2.26 and 2.29.

theorems.title: The bialternant formula
theorems.statement: For a partition λ of length at most n, the product of its Schur polynomial and the Vandermonde determinant equals the determinant with row exponents λᵣ+n−1−r, numbered from zero.
theorems.use: Summing marked columns records every shifted weight exactly once.
theorems.citation: R. P. Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics, vol. 2, §7.15, Theorem 7.15.1.

theorems.title: Values of definite algebraic modular forms
theorems.statement: For a definite group as in the cited proposition the class set at compact open level is finite. Evaluation gives the direct sum of the coefficient spaces invariant under the finite stabilizers of its representatives.
theorems.use: Expresses the definite Hecke trace as a sum of diagonal blocks.
theorems.citation: M. Greenberg and J. Voight, Lattice methods for algebraic modular forms on classical groups, Proposition 2.3 and Lemma 2.4.

theorems.title: Krasner’s lemma for a finite separable extension
theorems.statement: Over a complete nonarchimedean field, if an algebraic element is closer to a separable generator than any other conjugate of that generator, the field it generates contains the generator. Sufficiently small perturbations of a monic irreducible separable polynomial preserve its root fields up to conjugacy.
theorems.use: Polynomials with rational coefficients suffice to account for the finite extensions inside a fixed algebraic closure of the local coefficient field.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Propositions 7.60–7.61 and Corollary 7.62.

theorems.title: Integers and ramification in a finite local extension
theorems.statement: The valuation extends uniquely to a finite extension of a local field. Its ring of integers is a finite free module over the base valuation ring. A uniformizer of the base generates the power of the maximal ideal given by the ramification index.
theorems.use: A bound on the entries places the compact image in one finite module. The ramification index converts a valuation on the coefficient field to a power of the rational prime.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Proposition 2.29, Theorem 7.38, Corollary 7.42 and Remark 7.43.

theorems.title: The filtered de Rham comparison isomorphism
theorems.statement: For a de Rham representation, scalar extension identifies its invariant de Rham periods with the representation over the period field. The comparison and its inverse preserve the tensor product filtrations.
theorems.use: Applying the inverse in degree zero expresses each integral coordinate vector in the rescaled adapted basis.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Proposition 6.3.7.

theorems.title: The positive de Rham period ring
theorems.statement: The positive de Rham period ring is a complete discrete valuation ring. A generator of the kernel of Fontaine’s map after inverting the residue characteristic gives a uniformizer. Intersecting a power of the localized kernel ideal with the integral Witt ring recovers the corresponding integral power.
theorems.use: Powers of this uniformizer record the filtration orders of the individual period columns. Reduction modulo a power of the maximal ideal is unchanged by the defining completion.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Proposition 4.4.3, Corollary 4.4.5 and Proposition 4.4.6.

theorems.title: The invariant subfield of de Rham periods
theorems.statement: For a finite extension K of the local coefficient field ℚℓ, the elements of the de Rham period field fixed by the absolute Galois group of K are precisely K.
theorems.use: Two invariant bases for the same representation differ by an invertible matrix over K, hence by an integral unit in the positive de Rham ring.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Theorem 4.4.13.

theorems.title: Semistable representations and their de Rham periods
theorems.statement: For a semistable representation of the absolute Galois group of a finite extension K of ℚℓ, its semistable periods, after scalar extension from the maximal unramified subfield to K, identify with its de Rham periods.
theorems.use: The equality of dimensions permits the use of a filtration-adapted basis on each semistable layer.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Lemma 9.2.13.

theorems.title: Completeness and residues of the Witt ring
theorems.statement: For a perfect ring B of characteristic ℓ, W(B) is ℓ-torsion free, separated and complete for the ℓ-adic topology, with quotient B modulo ℓ. A unit is detected by its first Witt coordinate, and the first n Witt coordinates determine reduction modulo ℓⁿ.
theorems.use: These properties allow successive congruences of matrices to define one invertible matrix and give the exact number of truncated coefficients over a finite residue field.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, §4.2.

theorems.title: Stable images in a countable inverse system
theorems.statement: When the images from deeper levels eventually stabilize at each fixed level, the transition maps between these stable images are surjective. A compatible sequence can be built by lifting successively from a stable image.
theorems.use: Finite sets of truncated series give stabilization at each precision. Taking a level beyond two stabilization thresholds supplies the next lift of a prescribed column.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, §10.86, Definition 10.86.1, Example 10.86.2 and Lemma 10.86.3.

theorems.title: Finite submodules of a free module over a Bézout domain
theorems.statement: Over a Bézout domain, every finitely generated submodule of a free module is free of finite rank. Its rank is bounded by the rank of that free module.
theorems.use: The residual image is a submodule of k[[u]]ᵈ. The coefficient ring is Noetherian and principal, so the residual columns admit a finite basis.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 15.126.8(1).

theorems.title: The associated graded ring of a regular sequence
theorems.statement: If an ideal I of a ring B is generated by a regular sequence, the homogeneous degree-j part of its associated graded ring is freely generated over B/I by the monomials of degree j in the initial forms of that sequence.
theorems.use: The two regular pairs on the coefficient and period sides let one lift a residual basis one homogeneous degree at a time.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.69.2(1).

theorems.title: Krull’s intersection theorem for a finite module
theorems.statement: For a proper ideal I of a Noetherian local ring and a finite module M, the intersection of all IⁿM is zero.
theorems.use: Applying separatedness to the quotient by a Frobenius-transformed generator preserves divisibility on passage from finite period expansions to their limit.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Lemma 10.51.4.

theorems.title: Weierstrass preparation and division over a complete local ring
theorems.statement: Over a complete discrete valuation ring, a formal series with nonzero reduction is a unit times a uniquely determined monic distinguished polynomial. Division by a monic distinguished polynomial has a unique polynomial remainder of smaller degree.
theorems.use: Preparation turns Frobenius divisibility for a series into divisibility between polynomials, so it can be tested on their roots.
theorems.citation: R. Sharifi, Iwasawa Theory, Chapter 2, Proposition 2.2.1, Theorem 2.2.3 and Corollary 2.2.7.

theorems.title: Extending the absolute value of a complete discretely valued field
theorems.statement: The absolute value of a complete discretely valued field extends uniquely to every finite algebraic extension. Conjugate elements therefore have the same absolute value.
theorems.use: Every conjugate of the chosen maximal-norm root has the same norm. Taking an ℓth root strictly increases that norm and excludes a root of the distinguished factor.
theorems.citation: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem 7.38 and Corollary 7.40.

theorems.title: The integral crystalline period ring
theorems.statement: The ℓ-adically completed divided-power envelope of the kernel of Fontaine’s map contains the divided powers of its generators. It is a separated ℓ-adically complete, ℤℓ-flat domain.
theorems.use: The first two crystalline sections evaluate the divided powers of E. Torsion-freeness permits cancellation in the Galois defect and in the limiting trace comparison.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, §9.1, (9.1.1) and Proposition 9.1.1.

theorems.title: The fixed field in the crystalline period ring
theorems.statement: For a finite extension K of ℚℓ with maximal unramified subfield K₀, the elements of the crystalline period ring fixed by the local Galois group are exactly K₀.
theorems.use: In the basis of invariant columns, a vector is invariant precisely when its coordinates lie in this fixed field.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Theorem 9.1.5 and the calculation before Proposition 9.1.6.

theorems.title: Extending a coordinate functional from an independent set
theorems.statement: A linearly independent set in a vector space over a field extends to a basis. A functional defined on the span can be extended by assigning zero to each additional basis vector.
theorems.use: Taking a coefficient defines a retraction fixing the coefficient field and allows a coordinate to detect one trace discrepancy.
theorems.citation: Stacks Project, Chapter 11, §11.2. A maximal independent set is a basis by the basis-extension argument.

theorems.title: Regularity of the semistable period ring
theorems.statement: For a finite extension K of the ℓ-adic field with unramified subfield K₀, the semistable period ring is a domain, the fixed subfield of its fraction field is K₀, and each nonzero element spanning a stable ℓ-adic rational line is invertible in the ring.
theorems.use: Invariant fractions detect a dependence among invariant columns. Applying the stable-line assertion to their determinant makes the resulting basis invertible over the polynomial period ring.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Theorem 9.2.10 and Proposition 9.2.11.

theorems.title: Crystalline comparison and extension to the filtered de Rham module
theorems.statement: For a crystalline representation V over a finite local field K of residue characteristic ℓ, the comparison map gives a basis after extension to the crystalline period ring. Extending its invariant module from the unramified field to K identifies it with the filtered de Rham module.
theorems.use: The first comparison supplies invariant columns. The second supplies the adapted de Rham columns and inverse rows for the integral modification.
theorems.citation: O. Brinon and B. Conrad, CMI Summer School Notes on p-adic Hodge Theory, Proposition 9.1.9, p. 133.

theorems.title: Primitive element of a finite separable extension
theorems.statement: A finite separable field extension is generated by one element. In an algebraic closure its embeddings are in bijection with the distinct roots of the minimal polynomial of that generator.
theorems.use: A single operator on the space of unramified-linear functionals detects each coefficient embedding. The number of distinct roots is the field degree.
theorems.citation: The Stacks Project, Fields, Lemma 9.19.1 (primitive element).

theorems.title: The unramified quotient and arithmetic Frobenius
theorems.statement: For a local field with finite residue field the quotient of the absolute Galois group by inertia is the Galois group of the maximal unramified extension. This group is procyclic, topologically generated by arithmetic Frobenius.
theorems.use: On the finite set of coefficient embeddings, inertia and one Frobenius lift generate the image of the absolute Galois group. Their two transports therefore reach every embedding.
theorems.citation: R. Sharifi, Algebraic Number Theory, Propositions 6.4.8 and 6.4.10.

theorems.title: Multiplication of Iwahori double cosets
theorems.statement: At full Iwahori level, with the subgroup of volume one and residue field of size Q, the simple reflection indicator satisfies Tₛ²=(Q−1)Tₛ+Q·1. A reduced product of simple reflections gives the product of their indicators.
theorems.use: The quadratic identity inverts each simple operator over the complex numbers. Length-additive multiplication then inverts the finite permutation operators used to factor a diagonal translation.
theorems.citation: N. Iwahori and H. Matsumoto, On some Bruhat decomposition and the structure of the Hecke rings of p-adic Chevalley groups, Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS 25 (1965), §3.1, Theorem 3.3 and Proposition 3.4(i).

theorems.title: Schur orthogonality with probability Haar measure
theorems.statement: On a compact group with total Haar mass one, an irreducible unitary representation T of dimension d satisfies ∫|⟨v,T(k)u⟩|² dk = ‖v‖²‖u‖²/d. Matrix coefficients belonging to inequivalent compact types are orthogonal.
theorems.use: Compact character averaging projects onto a prescribed type. Applied to the residual at the identity, the same formula identifies the kernel as the compression of right translation.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof, Representations of Lie Groups, Lecture 2, §2.2, p. 16, orthogonality of matrix coefficients.

theorems.title: Weyl characters and determinant twists for the general linear group
theorems.statement: For an integral dominant weight w of GLₙ and an integer m such that w + (m,…,m) is a partition, the Schur polynomial of that partition at nonzero eigenvalues equals their product to the power m times the irreducible character of weight w. On distinct eigenvalues this follows directly from the quotient of alternants.
theorems.use: At one complex place this determinant twist cancels the rectangular character from the conjugate pair of weight factors. Homogeneity leaves the displayed power of the similitude multiplier.
theorems.citation: P. Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I & II, Theorem 26.4, Corollary 26.5 and §27.3 (the determinant representation).
